newsitem.title: USA: N.J. pension bond supporters rally on bus tour.
newsitem.headline: N.J. pension bond supporters rally on bus tour.

text.p: Supporters of New Jersey Gov. Christine Whitman's plan to borrow $2.8 billion of pension bonds traveled across the state Wednesday on a bus tour to promote the plan, but opponents said their next stop should be the ballot box.

Top Republican leaders traveled to four cities, with the last stop in Trenton with the governor. They argued that borrowing the money is the most fiscally responsible method of paying off the state's unfunded pension liability.
The plan would also allow New Jersey to avoid almost $600 million of contributions into the system, helping to balance the fiscal 1998 budget.
But opponents of the plan blasted the Governor's public relations effort, arguing that the idea should instead be placed directly to the voters in a referendum.

"It's going to take more than a one-day, four-stop bus tour to convince people that the $2.76 billion pension bond sale is anything more than an elaborate scheme to balance the state budget," state Sen. Gordon MacInnes, D-Morris, said in a statement.

"If the Governor and Republican supporters of this massive borrowing gimmick really want the public to come on board, they need to schedule another stop on their road trip -- the ballot box," MacInnes said.
